passage:
For three weeks I rehearsed what I would say to Neelam. My name is Gargi, and I don't let things go easily. Neelam had presented my poster idea to the fest committee as her own, and I found out from a stranger. I lost sleep, checked her stories and went cold with her in the corridor.

Then one evening on the terrace she said sorry, properly, without a "but". I noticed my shoulders drop. I told her, "I forgive you. That's for me, honestly, I'm tired of carrying it. But I'm not going to share unfinished ideas with you for a while." She nodded and said that was fair.

I didn't pretend it never happened. Our tea afterwards was quieter than before, and I was fine with that.

qa.q: How did Gargi find out about the poster idea?
Why did Gargi say the forgiveness was for herself?
qa.a: Because Gargi was tired of carrying the hurt. Gargi's shoulders dropped once the apology came.

qa.q: Why is forgiving while keeping a limit wiser than pretending nothing happened?
qa.a: It lets Gargi find peace now, while trust can be rebuilt slowly or not at all, without ignoring what Neelam did.

qa.q: How might Neelam have felt when Gargi set the limit?
qa.a: Perhaps disappointed but accepting. Neelam nodded and called it fair.

grounding: Gargi chooses to forgive a friend who hurt her for her own peace, without fully restoring trust.

Coach's note, university badminton squad, 12 March
Last month Pradeep dropped Shreya as his doubles partner two days before the zonal trials, by message, to play with a stronger player. It hurt her; she missed a week of practice.
Today Pradeep came to her after drills and apologised. I was restringing rackets nearby and saw it. Shreya listened with her arms folded, then said, "I forgive you. I'm not carrying this anymore. But I'm not ready to be partners again."
He asked if they were fine. She said, "We're okay. Not the same." She didn't pretend otherwise, and she didn't go cold either; she passed him the shuttle tube when he asked.
Afterwards she told me she forgave him for her own peace, because she was tired of being angry during matches. I have paired her with Tanushree for next week's friendlies and will keep Pradeep on a different court for now.

qa.q: When did Pradeep drop Shreya as his doubles partner?
qa.a: Two days before the zonal trials, by message.

qa.q: Why did Shreya choose to forgive Pradeep?
qa.a: For her own peace: she was tired of being angry during matches, though still hurt and wary.

qa.q: What did the coach do after watching the exchange?
qa.a: Paired Shreya with Tanushree for next week's friendlies and kept Pradeep on a different court for now.

qa.q: How might Pradeep feel after hearing "We're okay. Not the same"?
qa.a: Relieved to be forgiven but disappointed that the trust and the partnership aren't back.

grounding: Shows choosing to forgive a friend for one's own peace while trust is not fully restored, without pretending nothing happened.

passage:
Tuesday, late
Vinita sent me a long message tonight. Sorry, sorry, sorry. For telling Dhruv, of all people, that I had a crush on him, "as a joke", in front of the whole lab.
It's been three weeks. The old me would've replied "haha it's fine" and gone back to normal. That's what I did in school, and it always came back later as a stomach ache.
So I wrote back properly: "Thank you for apologising. I'm choosing to forgive you, because I don't want to keep carrying this. But I'm still hurt, and I'll take a bit of time before I tell you personal things again."
She replied: "That's fair. I'll wait."
I thought forgiving would feel like everything going back to how it was. It doesn't. It feels like putting down a heavy bag and walking lighter, without pretending the bag was never there.
— Salma

qa.a: That Salma had a crush on him, "as a joke", in front of the whole lab.

qa.q: How does Salma feel after choosing to forgive?
qa.a: Lighter, like putting down a heavy bag, while still hurt and cautious about sharing.

qa.q: Why was Salma's reply better than "haha it's fine"?
qa.a: It accepted the apology and forgave honestly while naming the hurt and a slower pace of trust, instead of burying it until it turned into a stomach ache.

qa.q: How might Vinita see Salma's reply?
qa.a: As fair even if it stings; she agrees to wait.

grounding: Illustrates deciding to forgive a friend for one's own peace while trust is still rebuilding, rather than pretending nothing happened.
